title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking
locator: Abstract, confidence association and qualitative findings
relevance: Self-reported effort and a shift toward checking and integration.
limitations: Survey association; not a causal demonstration of lost reading, attention or memory. Full paper not inspected in this topic pass.

title: Habitual use of GPS negatively impacts spatial memory during self-guided navigation
locator: PDF pages 1–2: abstract and participants; page 12: discussion caveats
relevance: Grounds the navigation analogy in a specific study.
limitations: Observational associations; 50-person main sample, 13-person unplanned follow-up; authors warn about strong conclusions. Not evidence about AI workplace reading.

title: Qur'an 96:1–5
authors: The Clear Quran translation by Mustafa Khattab
inspection: verse and Read in Context text
relevance: Textual anchor for the author’s reflection on Iqra.
limitations: A religious text and translation; the AI application is an authored reflection, not an empirical finding or a supplied scholarly ruling.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 3
locator: Book of Revelation, narration of Aisha concerning the cave of Hira
relevance: Traditional account of the first revelation and the instruction to read.
limitations: Retain religious context. Do not recast it as a technical rule about contemporary AI.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
locator: Abstract: parametric and non-parametric memory; retrieved passages
relevance: Technical starting point for distinguishing trained knowledge from supplied evidence.
limitations: Specific research architecture and tasks; no guarantee for every modern agent or for the correctness of a particular response.

title: The productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
relevance: Counterweight: benefits in speed and quality for bounded professional writing tasks.
limitations: June 2023 working-paper summary; publisher full text was unavailable in this pass. Does not measure recipient overload, reading or long-term learning.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
locator: Context retrieval and agentic search; Compaction; Structured note-taking
appraisal: Vendor design guidance: supports retrieval and compaction tradeoffs, not market prevalence or a diagnosis of an observed failure. No platform experiment was run here.

title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
authors: Barry Zhang, Keith Lazuka and Mahesh Murag
locator: The anatomy of a skill; Skills and the context window; Developing and evaluating skills
appraisal: Primary product/design description. Dynamic loading is documented; reliable compliance and improved results for this journal were not demonstrated.

title: Agent Skills specification
locator: Directory structure; Optional directories; Progressive disclosure
appraisal: Primary format specification, not an independent effectiveness study. Implementation behavior depends on the host. The format and S8 are related ecosystem sources, not two independent experiments.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
publisher: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics / ACL Anthology
locator: Original PDF pp. 157–161: abstract, controlled QA setup and results; pp. 167: conclusion
appraisal: Controlled context length/position changes; QA and synthetic retrieval. Historical model versions and bounded tasks limit generalization to current products. No test of skills, human cognition or compaction.

title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
authors: Philippe Laban, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yingbo Zhou and Jennifer Neville
locator: Publication-page abstract: simulated single/multi-turn comparison and early-assumption analysis
appraisal: Only author summary inspected; no full methods appraisal. Used to identify an alternative mechanism, without repeating effect sizes or attributing outcomes to context length or compaction.
